feature: One set of easing curves, named the same way everywhere
summary: Every screen in the study that asks how a value travels over time now offers the same eight named curves, in the same order, each drawing its own shape, ending in Draw a curve. It used to be four different lists, so the same control offered you Spring on one screen and not on the next.
setup: The design study on the dashboard, http://127.0.0.1:8791. Nothing to switch on. This is mock work, not app work, so there is nothing to try in Photonz itself.

try.do: Open the video editor page, http://127.0.0.1:8791/pages/video.html.
Click Graph on the Opacity row in the right panel, then click a diamond on the graph.
Click the curve name under Curve to next key and pick Ease out elastic.
Click Hold beside it, and watch the curve fade rather than disappear.
Open the punch-in walkthrough, pages/video-zoom-wt.html, and step to Ease the move.
Open pages/icon-animate-wt.html and step to the Curve row: same list, same order, same shapes.
Open pages/lang-motion.html and read the eight names beside the three motion tokens.

evaluate: Eight names plus Draw a curve: is that the right number, or does the everyday case want a shorter front door?
The shape is drawn beside every name. Do you pick by the picture or by the word?
Ease in out is the design language's --ease-standard, which is fast out and slow in, not CSS's symmetrical ease-in-out. Is that the right call, or should the name mean what CSS means?
On the video keyframe card, Hold sits beside the curve rather than inside the list. Does that read, or would you expect Hold among the curves?
A camera punch-in can now be given Ease out elastic and Steps, 4. Is one list worth offering curves video will rarely want?
rough: The screenshots are real browser renders of the study pages, not captures of the Photonz app: this task changed mocks and documentation only, no app code, so there is no walk to photograph.
Draw a curve opens the editor but its two handles do not drag anywhere: they are static in every mock that has them, including the icon pages this came from.
The video keyframe card's curve menu opens over the timeline because it is near the bottom of the panel. It is readable but it covers the lane you are editing.

Ease out elastic's cubic-bezier in the list is an approximation for CSS: the real curve is not a bezier at all, and the app samples it. Anything reading the css field for elastic gets a rough stand-in.
The speed ramp page still has its own Ramp / Hold control. That is a different question (how a speed stop joins the next one), not an easing vocabulary, so it was deliberately left alone.
